[03_exclusions#4]
What is not covered. Claims for excluded treatment are normally declined. You can appeal a decline; see "Appeals and complaints".

[03_exclusions#2]
What is not covered. - Cosmetic procedures, for example teeth whitening or cosmetic surgery. - Routine dental care, for example check-ups, cleaning and fillings. - Routine optical care: eye tests, glasses and contact lenses. - Alternative therapies, for example acupuncture and homeopathy. - Fitness and wellness classes, for example yoga, pilates and gym membership. This applies even if a class is described as therapeutic or is run at a clinic. - Treatment received outside Ireland.

[03_exclusions#3]
What is not covered. If a receipt includes an excluded item alongside a covered one, the claim is reviewed by a claims assessor.

Cover and annual limits. At the limit. A claim for exactly the limit, for example 60 for a GP visit, is within the limit.

Cover and annual limits. Above the limit. If a receipt is for more than the limit, the claim is reviewed by a claims assessor. Any claim for more than 1,000 is also reviewed by an assessor.

[05_pre_authorisation#6]
Pre-authorisation. Other treatment. GP visits, consultant visits, physiotherapy and prescriptions do not need pre-authorisation, but consultant visits and physiotherapy need a referral. See "Cover and annual limits".
